resources.string: Privacy mode is on. Debrief, Compare, and AI Export hide the last half of each MAC, the coordinates, and a Remote ID id. The log and sit export still have the full addresses and coordinates.
A sit is the radios heard during a named stretch of time. Path, Debrief, and Compare use the open sit, a saved sit you pick, or the last 15 minutes.
No sit is running. Path and Debrief use the last 15 minutes until you start one.
No sit is running. Path and Debrief use the sit you pick.
Uses what is still in memory, not a saved sit.
End this sit to pick a saved one.

North is up. The line is this phone, with times along it. Black is the start. Blue is you. One icon is one radio. A number is several radios in one spot. A thick green stretch is a stay. An advertised position is the last one that radio sent. A red diamond is where this phone was during a GNSS detection.
Turn on Tag detections with GPS and walk, or pick a sit that recorded a path.
Tap a number for the radios there. Tap one icon for that radio. Tap a row to open it. Tap a red diamond for that detection.
= advertised track within 2 km of this path
= one advertised position within 2 km of this path
= where this phone was during a GNSS detection
No alerts with a GPS stamp on this path.

Leaves unmatched Bluetooth radios that keep changing address out of the Debrief lists. The counts still include them. Extra attention, named signatures, bookmarks, and radios that sent a position stay. Sit export still has every radio.

Debrief and Compare open with counts. A radio is listed when it is Extra attention, has a custom name, is marked Mine, or is bookmarked. Compare also lists a decoded value that changed. Turn this on for the full list. The PDF draws the counts as bars. Sit export still has every radio.
A short note for pasting into a chat: rates, signal bands, Extra attention, and tracking ids. It does not repeat the Debrief lists. A one-radio export is on that radio’s page.

One row per radio in this sit, or the last 15 minutes. Not the log. CSV and JSON include the matched signatures. GPX and KML include this phone’s path and a point for each detection. Fieldwatch does not upload the file. Privacy mode does not hide addresses in it.
This sit: %1$s. Same window as Debrief.
This sit: the last 15 minutes still in memory, about 400 radios. Same window as Debrief.
Save a second sit to compare. Start a sit, then end it. The last 15 minutes can be this sit.

The same report as text or PDF. Radios only in this sit, only in the second, and in both. Extra attention and named radios are marked. These points are where this phone was, not a location from the other radio.
A short note on what overlaps and what is only in one sit. It does not repeat the compare lists. The sit-report export stays on this window only.
Unmatched radios in the log that share an id. Not every unknown radio. Nothing is added until you save it.
%1$d lines this session · %2$d KB on disk

The file on disk is one detection per line. CSV is those rows in a spreadsheet. GPX, KML, and WiGLE are points where this phone was when it heard each radio, not a location from the other radio. Tag detections with GPS and logging both have to be on. Share uses the Android share sheet. Fieldwatch does not upload.
Deletes the log files on this phone. This cannot be undone. Scanning starts a new empty log.
Debrief and AI Export use this window until you end it. The Live list is unchanged.
Removes the saved sit from this phone. The log is unchanged.
Removes saved sits from this phone. An open sit is not deleted. The log is unchanged.
%1$s. Same window as Path. Moving with you runs when Tag detections with GPS is on and you have moved. This is not a legal finding.

Opens this app’s battery page. Turn on Allow background usage there. If it is off, Android can stop the scan when you leave.

Saves switches, filters, presets, named radios, and signature watches. Not the catalog, and not logs. The catalog is Export signatures, above. Import replaces those items on this phone and leaves the catalog. Fieldwatch asks before a file turns the TAK feed on or changes where it sends.
This opens Fieldwatch’s battery page. Turn on Allow background usage. Fieldwatch matches it when you come back.
Choose Unrestricted. On some phones, including Samsung, tap the words Allow background usage, then choose Unrestricted. Fieldwatch matches it when you come back.

A double pip on the media volume when a watched radio first appears, or comes back after leaving. It does not repeat while that radio stays in view. You can use the beep, the voice, or both. Turn the media volume up if you hear nothing, then tap Test alert.
Phone, Android version, the scan switches, and whether Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, and Location are on. Copy pastes that into an issue. Network names and GPS coordinates are left out.
The popup, red line, beep, and voice start at this level. A weaker hit still shows in Diagnostics and in the sit report.
The same pip as a watchlist hit, on the media volume. The popup and the red line still show if this is off.
Stand outside, hold still, and stay away from a router. This takes about a minute. The result stays on this phone until you calibrate again. It is not part of Export settings.
Calibrate this phone before turning the check on.

Detects interference and spoofing of GNSS (GPS) satellites. Interference can also be caused by other nearby electronics, such as Wi-Fi routers. Fieldwatch cannot tell the source or the distance. A hit already under way when the check starts can be missed. A hit opens a popup. After you dismiss it, a red line stays on Live until it ends.
Watches for satellites fading at the same time. A hand, a pocket, or getting in a car can do that. Leave this off unless you are testing it.
Keeps the GPS receiver awake instead of letting it rest. Uses more battery. Android 12 and newer. Older phones ignore this.
A few phones report gain backwards. Turn this on only if a Wi-Fi router makes the AGC number in Diagnostics go up.
A silent notification for this warning. The popup and the red line still show if this is off. Separate from the watchlist switch.
Low waits for a deeper drop. High alerts on a smaller drop, including some routers.

Watches for gain falling while the signal holds or rises. A clock or position mismatch counts with that, or with another mismatch. One mismatch alone does not warn. A careful spoofer can still get past these checks.
Says possible GPS interference, or possible GPS spoofing. It speaks again only when the level goes up. Uses the media volume. Separate from the watchlist Voice switch.
Live scrolls to a new watched radio so you can see the flash. Turn this off if you do not want the list to move.
Keeps the screen awake while Live is in front.
%1$d lines this session · %2$d KB on disk. Share, Save, and Reset / clear log are on the Reports tab.
The file on disk is one detection per line. Reports → Log can share or save CSV, JSON, GPX, KML, or WiGLE.
Logging is off. Scanning still runs. Nothing new is written until you turn this on.
Logging is on. New detections are added to the file.
A name for one MAC. Alert is optional. Filters → Named radios shows them on Live. Signature watches stay on the Signatures tab.
Dark theme for low light. With this off, Fieldwatch follows the system setting.

With internet, Debrief turns coordinates into a street and city, and Reports → Path loads a map under the trace. Nothing is sent to a Fieldwatch server. Offline, Debrief keeps the coordinates and Path stays a plain trace. Turn this off to leave streets and the map out.
Hides the last half of each MAC, the coordinates, and Remote ID ids in Debrief, Compare, and AI Export. The log and the sit export keep everything. The TAK feed pauses.

Replaces the stock catalog, colors, stock bookmarks, stock filters, and the default switches. Signatures and filters you added are deleted. Export those first if you want a backup. This cannot be undone.
Save settings to SD card / storage…
Save signatures to SD card / storage…
Battery saver scans less often and sleeps between rounds. Performance scans Wi-Fi as fast as Android allows.
Waiting for Android to run the next Wi-Fi scan…
Shows the Live tour again: display, pause, filters, signatures, reports, and settings.

Export shares the catalog, including signatures you added. Import adds rows and does not delete any. Update from GitHub refreshes the stock signatures and leaves yours, your bookmarks, and your settings. It needs internet. Restore defaults deletes the signatures you added.
A silent notification when a watched radio appears. The beep and the flash are enough for most sits.

Stamps this phone’s position on each detection: Live detail, Moving with you, Debrief, and new log rows. That is where you were, not a location from the other radio. Use high-accuracy location, or the path stays empty. Heard-here TAK pins need this. Remote ID uses the coordinates in the advertisement. Turn this off to keep your position out of the logs.

Sends map markers to ATAK, WinTAK, or iTAK. Radios you hear are pinned at this phone’s GPS, at the loudest point, and labeled (here). Walking away does not move the pin. A louder detection does. Remote ID aircraft use the coordinates in the advertisement. An operator location is a second pin: the takeoff spot, the pilot, or a fixed point. A radio that leaves keeps its name for How long a spot stays. Tap a marker for the name, MAC, and signal. This is not direction finding. Privacy mode pauses the feed.
Privacy mode is on, so the feed is paused. Turn Privacy mode off to send markers.
Opens the same battery page. Choose Unrestricted. On some phones, including Samsung, tap Allow background usage first, then choose Unrestricted.

Speaks the watch on the same volume as the beep. You can use the beep, the voice, or both. A second hit is skipped if Fieldwatch is already speaking. With no speech engine, the beep still plays if Beep is on.
Beep, voice, flash, and the jump when a bookmarked signature or named radio appears. If this is off, bookmarks stay, and Fieldwatch stays quiet.

Class is the group on Live, such as finder tags or audio. Signature is the catalog name, such as Apple AirTags. Class + signature says both. A named radio with Alert on always says the name you gave it.
Wi-Fi and Bluetooth only. Android does not show phones that are only connected to an access point. Fieldwatch sees access points and Bluetooth advertisers.
This opens Developer options. Turn Wi-Fi scan throttling off. Fieldwatch matches that switch when you come back.
This opens Developer options. Turn Wi-Fi scan throttling on to use the normal wait. Fieldwatch matches that switch when you come back.
This phone is older than Android 11, so Fieldwatch cannot tell if Wi-Fi scan throttling is on. Faster scanning stays off.
Off. Android is limiting Wi-Fi scans to about four per two minutes. Tap the switch to open Developer options.
On. A new access-point list about every 8 seconds. Uses more battery. This matches Wi-Fi scan throttling in Developer options.
This phone is older than Android 11, so Fieldwatch cannot tell if Wi-Fi scan throttling is on. The switch stays off.
Cut noise: radio types, signature classes, new radios, and moving with you.
Freezes the display. Scanning and logging keep running.

This phone is ATAK on this handset, at %1$s:%2$d. LAN multicast is %3$s:%4$d, for other ATAK apps on this Wi-Fi. Custom is one address. UDP only. A TAK server on TCP 8087 is not this feed. If This phone shows no pins, use Custom with the Wi-Fi address at the bottom of Settings and port %5$d.
UDP. This phone uses %1$d. LAN multicast uses %2$d. Not TCP 8087.

Turn on any combination. Extra attention sends body cameras, glasses, recorders, pentest gear, and public-safety access points. Payload location sends Remote ID and any radio that advertises its own coordinates. Watchlist sends bookmarked signatures and named radios with Alert on. All signatures sends every labeled radio, which is noisy in a crowd. Unmatched radios are never sent. A pin needs coordinates, from the advertisement or from Tag detections with GPS.

After a radio leaves, the spot keeps its name for this long. The time starts when it leaves. Until deleted stays until the feed is turned off. This phone’s Fieldwatch marker stays for about 2 minutes.

A mark on the map where this phone was, and a line on this phone’s Fieldwatch marker. A short hit is a pin. A hit that continues while the phone moves becomes an ellipse from the start to the last place it was heard, half as wide as it is long. The mark does not say where the cause is. Off sends nothing. While alerting sends during a hit at or above Alert from. Red line also keeps the line for the 10 minutes after. The ellipse stops growing when the hit ends. Any hit also sends a Low detection that never shows the red line. This phone needs a GPS fix.
The time starts at the last update. Until deleted stays until GNSS is set to Off.

Adds a note to this phone’s Fieldwatch marker when a flood is detected, until the flood ends. Not its own pin. This does not change the red line on Live. A store full of radios advertising pairing can cause this. The note does not say it was one radio, and it does not name a tool. This phone needs a GPS fix.
